image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align over the orange can for a gentle touch/lift test; its fill state is not visually known.
Descend with open fingers to straddle the upper orange can without contacting the table.
Gently close around the orange can before a short test lift; commanded opening alone does not establish a grasp.
Short vertical test lift of the orange can; inspect its retention and motion under contact.
Orange is visibly lifted. Ease to a near-contact opening over its original spot to test whether it slips under its weight.
Continue easing the orange-can grip in small increments; observe weight-induced slipping rather than trusting the commanded aperture.
Orange slipped at the looser setting. Move above the blue can for a comparable gentle grasp test; fill identity remains uncertain.
Lower open fingers around the upper blue can, matching the orange-can test height.
Close gently on the blue can for a comparable test lift.
Lift the blue can a short distance vertically and inspect retention before easing contact.
Ease the blue-can grip to a near-contact opening and watch for slipping under its weight.
Blue fell at the eased opening. Return over orange to compare retention at the same opening before selecting the lighter can.
Straddle orange at the same grasp height used for blue, preparing a matched retention test.
Gently regrasp orange; earlier touch tests suggest it retained contact longer than blue, but verify before transport.
Raise orange a short distance over its original location and inspect its grasp before the final loose-contact test.
Ease orange to light contact and pause, checking whether it stays suspended rather than assuming the gripper target measures weight.
Orange slipped at 0.8 opening. Return to its standing grasp height for a more precise light-contact test.
Test a 0.76 opening on orange with a short lift; compare actual can motion rather than interpreting opening as force.
Orange rose with the light-contact grasp. Set it down gently before testing blue with exactly the same opening.
Release the supported orange can, lift clear, and move toward blue for the matched light-contact test.
Center over blue and lower open fingers to the same upper-can grasp height.
Use the same 0.76 light-contact opening on blue and attempt a short lift, comparing visible retention with orange.
Blue also lifts at 0.76. Test slightly lighter contact over its original spot; the weight comparison is still uncertain.
Hold the light-contact blue grasp steady to distinguish sustained support from transient retention.
Blue slipped to the table at 0.775. Move to orange to repeat precisely that sustained light-contact test.
Lower to orange's upper-can grasp height, keeping the test geometry consistent.
Lift orange with the same 0.76 contact setting used for blue before the sustained 0.775 comparison.
Apply the same 0.775 light-contact test to orange, watching for the slip seen with blue.
Orange slipped more quickly than blue at the same loose setting. Reposition for a slightly tighter sustained-contact comparison.
Test orange with a 0.765 opening and a short vertical lift, keeping it over its original spot.
Pause the orange test lift at fixed light contact to measure visible slip over time.
Check orange at the midpoint contact setting, 0.770, to finish the slip-threshold comparison.
Orange visibly slips at 0.770. Set it down, release, and clear the can before testing blue at that setting.
Move clear of orange and descend around blue for the final matched light-contact comparison.
Grasp and lift blue at 0.76 before repeating orange's slipping threshold test.
Hold blue at the 0.770 contact setting where orange slipped, comparing visible support over time.
Regrasp blue securely. Both slip near this aperture, but the earlier slower blue slip is the best available evidence that it is lighter; identification remains uncertain.
Lift blue securely above the other can and basket rim, checking visible retention before transfer.
Blue remains visibly retained. Carry it left toward the basket at clearance height.
Finish moving the retained blue can over the basket opening, slowing near its center.
